definition.title: Subclassical Calculus
definition.para: A calculus C is subclassical with respect to a background calculus B if every sequent derivable in C is derivable in B, but there exists at least one sequent derivable in B that is not derivable in C. The graph takes Gentzen's classical sequent calculus LK as the canonical background. A subclassical calculus is therefore a restriction: it forbids at least one inference that LK licenses, whether by omitting a structural rule (as in linear logic, which removes both Weakening and Contraction), by restricting the multiplicity of conclusions (as in intuitionistic logic LJ, which permits at most one formula on the right of the turnstile), or by some combination of rule modifications.
